page: Google Cloud Platform c2-standard-30 is a compute-optimized virtual machine powered by a 3.1 GHz Intel Xeon x86_64 processor. The configuration allocates 30 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 15 physical cores with two threads per core. Cache resources include 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 24 MB of shared L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, and cryptographic AES acceleration, tailored for vector mathematics and calculation-heavy tasks.

System memory consists of 120.0 GB of RAM, establishing a ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. PassMark memory testing places this instance in the top 25 percent tier, supported by uncached memory read bandwidth of 113.91 GB/sec and uncached write bandwidth of 48.85 GB/sec. The instance includes no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage volumes for file systems and databases, and provides no dedicated GPU accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent middle-tier performance across general compute evaluations, recording 30,787.06 in stress-ng multi-core tests and a PassMark CPU score of 28,652.35. In application metrics, the server delivers 27.0 million Redis SET operations per second and 18.82 GB/sec in static web throughput. Natural language model inference handles small 135M models at 92.83 generation tokens per second, but throughput drops significantly on larger architectures, recording 4.37 tokens per second on 70B model prompt processing.

The hardware profile offers balanced cost efficiency for tasks requiring predictable dedicated compute cores combined with upper-tier memory throughput. Tradeoffs include the complete absence of local NVMe storage and limited efficiency for heavy transformer-based machine learning models. Recommended workloads include multi-threaded software compilation, high-concurrency web serving, intermediate in-memory caching layers, and high-performance batch computing.
